title: Five beads held by abandoned bd-spin agent claims cannot be closed without --force
description:
Found while reconciling the duplicated-bead pairs (PKIX-29bc follow-on work, 2026-11-25).

Five beads carry an assignee of the form 'bd-spin/bd-spin-<timestamp>-<pid>', an agent identity from May 2026 that was never released:

  PKIX-jbvb      blocked   bd-spin-20260513T202312Z-3017126
  PKIX-jbvb.9.1  open      bd-spin-20260514T024333Z-3287470
  PKIX-hbzo      open      bd-spin-20260511T212242Z-1478141
  PKIX-ng0x      blocked   bd-spin-20260511T043138Z-4160815
  PKIX-xj81      blocked   bd-spin-20260511T043138Z-4160815

The practical effect is a trap rather than a cosmetic wart: bd refuses both 'bd unclaim' and 'bd close' on a bead held by a different actor, so anyone finishing this work hits 'cannot close: assignee is bd-spin/..., actor is <you>; reclaim or use --force to override' and has to know about --force. PKIX-gphz.1 was in the same state and blocked closing a duplicate until force-unclaimed.

Note the two sharing 4160815: one crashed agent took both PKIX-ng0x and PKIX-xj81 and never came back.

Fix is mechanical -- 'bd unclaim <id> --force' on each -- but it is someone's deliberate call rather than a sweep to run blind, because releasing a claim is a statement that nobody is working the item. Six months of silence from an agent process ID is good evidence of that, and the claims should probably just go.

Worth checking at the same time whether anything in the workflow re-creates these: if an agent run claims beads and exits without unclaiming, the board accumulates this indefinitely. A crash-safe claim (lease with expiry) would be the real fix; 'bd doctor' may already have an opinion.
